chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'They report from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that charity is not permissible for the rich, nor for the one with strong resources.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not correct for the rich.'
ai.seo_question: Who is eligible to receive Zakat according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refines the general prophetic tradition by specifying that the prohibition of receiving Zakat applies strictly to the 'rich' (al-Ghani), thereby distinguishing them from the 'strong' (Dhi Mirrah Siwwi) who may be eligible. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise legal categorization within the eight categories of Zakat recipients, ensuring that those with sufficient means for self-sufficiency are excluded while others with varying degrees of capability may still qualify.
